Course description

Home Economics prepares students to teach and practice skills used at home, in work, and in small business. The program combines classroom learning with hands-on laboratory work.

Food preparation
Cooking, nutrition, and food technology.
Customer service
Hospitality and workplace skills.
Housekeeping
Household resources and consumer education.
Clothing and crafts
Construction, design, and handicrafts.
Personal care
Family relationships and well-being.
Livelihood
Entrepreneurship for employment or self-employment.

Graduates are trained as TLE teachers and can also pursue TESDA National Certificates to support employment or their own business.
